item.title: Core Concepts MOC
item.description:
Core Concepts MOC

This Map of Content (MOC) serves as a central hub for fundamental technical concepts in distributed systems, microservices, and event-driven architecture.

Distributed Systems

  • [[CAP Theorem]] - Understanding the trade-offs between Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance
  • [[Consistency Models]] - Strong, eventual, and causal consistency
  • [[Partitioning and Sharding]] - Strategies for distributing data across multiple nodes

Microservices Architecture

  • [[Service Discovery]] - How services find and communicate with each other
  • [[API Gateways]] - Central entry point for client applications
  • [[Circuit Breakers]] - Handling failures gracefully in distributed systems

Event-Driven Architecture

  • [[Event Sourcing]] - Using events as the source of truth
  • [[CQRS]] - Command Query Responsibility Segregation
  • [[Message Brokers]] - Understanding message queues and pub/sub systems

Key Concepts by Topic

Distributed Systems Fundamentals

  • Consensus Algorithms
  • Distributed Transactions
  • Replication Strategies
  • Failure Detection
  • Clock Synchronization

Microservices Patterns

  • Service Mesh
  • Backend for Frontend (BFF)
  • Bulkhead Pattern
  • Sidecar Pattern
  • Database per Service

Event-Driven Patterns

  • Event-Driven Integration
  • Event Streaming
  • Event Sourcing
  • Saga Pattern
  • Outbox Pattern

Related MOCs

  • [[020-Technologies MOC]] - Specific technologies implementing these concepts
  • [[030-Repositories MOC]] - Code examples and implementations
  • [[040-Projects MOC]] - Projects utilizing these concepts

Resources and References

  • Distributed Systems by Martin Kleppmann
  • Building Microservices by Sam Newman
  • Designing Data-Intensive Applications

item.title: Maps of Content (MOC): Interview Preparation Knowledge Base
item.description:
Maps of Content (MOC): Interview Preparation Knowledge Base

Welcome to my Knowledge Base! This post serves as a central navigation hub for all the content on this site. It’s structured to help you easily find and connect related concepts for backend engineering and interview preparation.

Core Knowledge Areas

Core Concepts

Fundamental technical concepts that form the foundation of distributed systems and modern backends.

  • Distributed Systems

    • CAP Theorem in Distributed Systems
    • Consistency Models (Coming soon)
    • Partitioning and Sharding (Coming soon)

  • Microservices

    • Service Discovery (Coming soon)
    • API Gateways (Coming soon)
    • Circuit Breakers (Coming soon)

  • Event-Driven Architecture

    • CQRS (Coming soon)
    • Event Sourcing (Coming soon)
    • Message Brokers (Coming soon)

Technologies

Deep dives into specific technologies used in backend development.

  • Redis

    • Redis Data Structures and Use Cases
    • Redis Patterns (Coming soon)
    • Redis Performance Optimization (Coming soon)

  • Databases

    • Cassandra Data Modeling (Coming soon)
    • PostgreSQL Performance Tuning (Coming soon)
    • MongoDB Best Practices (Coming soon)

  • Message Brokers

    • Kafka Architecture (Coming soon)
    • RabbitMQ Patterns (Coming soon)
    • Pulsar vs Kafka (Coming soon)

Interview Preparation

Materials specifically designed to help you prepare for technical interviews.

  • System Design

    • Scaling a Notification Service
    • Designing a URL Shortener (Coming soon)
    • Building a Distributed Cache (Coming soon)

  • Coding Problems

    • Common Data Structure Problems (Coming soon)
    • Concurrency Challenges (Coming soon)
    • Algorithm Patterns (Coming soon)

How to Use This Knowledge Base

There are multiple ways to navigate this site:

  1. Start with the MOCs: Use this and other Maps of Content as starting points
  2. Browse by Category: Explore content organized by main categories
  3. Follow Series: Dive deep into a specific topic following a progressive series
  4. Search by Tags: Find related content across different categories

Content Principles

This knowledge base follows these principles:

  1. Interconnected: Content is linked to help you see relationships between concepts
  2. Practical: Theoretical concepts are supported by practical examples
  3. Interview-focused: Designed to prepare you for technical interviews
  4. Evolving: Regularly updated with new content and improvements

Contribution

Have a suggestion? Found an error? Would like to see a specific topic? Feel free to reach out or contribute!
